_anchor.title: The mid-market engagement
_anchor.terms: Outline & Co. delivers the strategy → identity → digital product flow for mid-market companies on fixed-price engagement scopes agreed at pitch. Standard engagement: 12-16 weeks. Standard deliverables: positioning document, identity system, digital product artefact (website, app, or design system).

new_end_users.label: Returning client
new_end_users.rationale: A new client category that opens up only if the studio first builds a way to keep prior-engagement context queryable. Without that, refresh engagements 18-24 months after handover stay too expensive to win — every one of them starts from scratch.

anchors.label: Strategy → identity → digital product, on time, on fixed price
anchors.description: The cardinal user need: a mid-market client receives the studio's signature flow as a single coherent package, delivered in 12-16 weeks at a price agreed at pitch.

components.label: Strategy
components._description: Brand strategy area. Positioning, audience research, naming, narrative workshops, competitive audits.

components.label: Design
components._description: Brand identity area. Identity systems, visual languages, brand books, motion systems.

components.label: Digital product
components._description: Digital product area. UI design for B2B web and apps; design systems for client product teams; embedded UX research.

components.label: Client services
components._description: Client services area. Kickoff workshops, weekly check-ins, asset handovers, scoping for new pitches.

components.label: Audience research
components._description: Interview the client's customers and stakeholders, transcribe and synthesise into an insights document feeding positioning.
components._body:
The strategy lead and one strategist run the audience-research interviews for an engagement. They transcribe and synthesise into an insights document that feeds [brand positioning](brand-positioning.md) (outline-roles-2025).

The four mid-level strategists run interviews and transcripts on assigned engagements; each strategist runs roughly four engagements per year, in parallel rather than serial (outline-roles-2025).
components.ai_effect: Interview transcript and synthesis become assisted. The strategist still runs the room.

top_matches.task: confer with clients to determine objectives, budget, background information, and presentation approaches, styles, and techniques.
analyze patrons' requests to determine needed information and assist in furnishing or locating that information.
collect information about clients through interviews, observation, or tests.

components.label: Brand positioning
components._description: Author the positioning document for an engagement: how the client should be understood, against whom, with what proof points.
components._body:
The strategy lead writes the positioning document for every engagement. Inputs come from [audience research](audience-research.md) and the [competitive audit](competitive-audit.md); the output is a written brief that the [design lead](../people/lena-thorvaldsen.md) builds the identity system on top of (outline-roles-2025, outline-charter-2024 §1).

The artefact is owned by [Marco Bellini](../people/marco-bellini.md) and is not delegated — every positioning document goes out under his signature (outline-roles-2025).
components.ai_effect: AI assists evidence-gathering. Marco still authors the document.

top_matches.task: confer with colleagues to formulate positions and strategies pertaining to pending issues.
Administer, coordinate, or recommend disciplinary and corrective actions.
prepare written documents to establish contracts with or communicate financial recommendations to clients.

components.label: Competitive audit
components._description: Map a client's competitive landscape: who else exists in the category, what they sound like, where the white space is.
components._body:
Strategists write competitive audits on briefed projects: who else exists in the category, what they sound like, where the white space is. The audit feeds the positioning brief (outline-roles-2025).

The strategy lead also does competitive-audit work for new pitches when the studio is in front of a prospect — the audit is the pitch's evidence base (outline-roles-2025).
components.ai_effect: Web scrape plus summarization is where AI crushes it. The audit becomes a prompt, not a week.

top_matches.task: Identify prospective customers, using business directories, leads from existing clients, participation in organizations, or trade show or conference attendance.
identify prospective customers using business directories, leads from existing clients, participation in organizations, or trade show or conference attendance.
identify prospective customers by using business directories, following leads from existing clients, participating in organizations and clubs, and attending trade shows and conferences.

components.label: Brand book
components._description: Author the brand book — the studio's signature artefact. Built personally by the design lead on every engagement.
components._body:
The design lead builds the brand book personally on every engagement. The brand book is the artefact the studio is best known for and the design lead does not delegate it (outline-roles-2025).

Mid-level designers may produce individual brand-book chapters under the lead's review, but the integration into a single artefact is the lead's hand (outline-roles-2025).
components.ai_effect: Lena's hand. AI doesn't write the brand book.

top_matches.task: collaborate with graphic artists, editors and writers to produce master copies according to design specifications.
make manuscript acceptance or revision recommendations to the publisher.
Manage inventory or sale of artist merchandise.

components.label: Identity system build
components._description: Build the full identity system for an engagement: typography, colour, grid, motion, illustration direction, photo direction.
components._body:
Senior designers run the identity-system build for individual engagements: typography, colour, grid, motion logic, illustration direction, photo direction. They typically own one engagement at a time (outline-roles-2025).

Mid-level designers support the senior on the system build. The design lead reviews every deliverable before it leaves the studio per the senior-eyes-on-every-output rule (outline-roles-2025, outline-charter-2024 §9).
components.ai_effect: System-component generation (type pairs, colour scales) becomes assisted; the senior designer reviews.

top_matches.task: design complex graphics and animation, using independent judgment, creativity, and computer equipment.
create designs, concepts, and sample layouts, based on knowledge of layout principles and esthetic design concepts.
integrate and develop visual elements, such as line, space, mass, color, and perspective, to produce desired effects, such as the illustration of ideas, emotions, or moods.

components.label: Visual language
components._description: Define the visual language for an engagement: typography, colour, imagery direction, motion logic, on top of the positioning brief.
components._body: The design lead defines the visual language for the brief from strategy: typography choice, colour direction, imagery treatment, motion logic. The visual language feeds the [identity system build](identity-system-build.md) (outline-roles-2025).
components.ai_effect: Lena's hand. AI doesn't define a visual language.

top_matches.task: integrate and develop visual elements, such as line, space, mass, color, and perspective, to produce desired effects, such as the illustration of ideas, emotions, or moods.
formulate basic layout design or presentation approach and specify material details, such as style and size of type, photographs, graphics, animation, video, and sound.
interpret engineering sketches, specifications, or drawings.

components.label: Design system build
components._description: Build a design system for clients who maintain their own product engineering. Documented system, ready for client handoff.
components._body:
Mid-level product designers own design-system documentation when the client is building a system the studio will hand off. The senior product designer leads the system architecture; the mid-level produces the documentation that lets the client team maintain it (outline-roles-2025).

The system build feeds the [asset handover](asset-handover.md) ritual at the end of the engagement.
components.ai_effect: Documentation auto-generated from the system. The mid-level designer becomes a curator.

top_matches.task: Discuss the design with the client.
prepare design presentations and proposals for staff or customers.
Provide feedback to product design teams so that products can be tailored to clients' needs.

components.label: UI design
components._description: UI design for B2B web and apps: screens, components, interactions, accessibility, paired with client front-end engineers.
components._body:
Senior product designers own UI design for individual engagements: screens, components, interactions, prototyping, accessibility audits, pairing with the client's front-end developers (outline-roles-2025).

The product lead reviews every UI deliverable; on enterprise engagements the lead or a senior typically embeds with the client product team for the duration (outline-roles-2025, outline-charter-2024 §16).
components.ai_effect: UI generation drifts to commodity fast. The differentiator becomes the brief upstream, not the screens.

top_matches.task: Conceptualize and help design interfaces for multimedia games, products, and devices.
design customer interface of online storefront, using web programming or e-commerce software.
Research and apply innovative solutions for product design, visuals, and user experience to meet the needs of individual Web development projects.

components.label: UX research
components._description: Embedded UX research with the client product team: usability testing, observation, synthesis.
components._body:
The product lead runs UX research when the engagement asks for it: embedded with the client's product team, usability testing, observation, synthesis into a research report (outline-roles-2025).

User insights from research feed back into [UI design](ui-design.md) and into the [positioning](brand-positioning.md) brief on engagements where the strategy work hasn't yet closed.
components.ai_effect: Synthesis assisted; interviews and observation still need a human in the room.

top_matches.task: Assess the user-interface or usability characteristics of products.
research and test new or modified hardware or software products to determine performance and interoperability.
provide feedback and recommendations to developers on software usability and functionality.

components.label: Asset handover
components._description: Run the asset-handover ritual at the end of each engagement: delivery of all artefacts, sign-off, archival.
components._body:
The client services lead manages the asset-handover ritual at the end of each engagement. The handover package collects the brand book, identity system files, design-system documentation, UI screens, and any source files the client owns under the contract (outline-roles-2025).

The relevant discipline lead is present at handover; the lead and Tomás together walk the client through what they're receiving and confirm sign-off (outline-roles-2025).
components.ai_effect: Package auto-assembles from delivered files. Tomás reviews and signs off.

Coordinate the removal of sets, props, and exhibits after productions or events are complete.
recommend actions related to historical art, such as which items to add to a collection or which items to display in an exhibit.

components.label: Kickoff workshop
components._description: Run the kickoff workshop for every engagement: scope agreement, calendar, weekly cadence, single point of contact on client side.
components._body:
The client services lead runs the kickoff workshop for every engagement: scoping, calendar, weekly cadence agreement, single point of contact on the client side. The output is the engagement-scope document that anchors weekly check-ins, asset handovers, and the fixed-price agreement (outline-roles-2025, outline-charter-2024 §4, §12).

The relevant discipline lead sits at the kickoff alongside [Tomás Reis](../people/tomas-reis.md). Enterprise kickoffs additionally include the founder (outline-roles-2025).
components.ai_effect: Agenda and scoping assisted; the discipline lead still anchors the conversation.

top_matches.task: Schedule promotional or performance engagements for clients.
meet with clients to schedule and plan details of conventions, banquets, receptions and other functions.
plan, organize, and conduct practice sessions.

components.label: Weekly check-in
components._description: Run the weekly check-in call on each active engagement: progress, blockers, next-week scope confirmation.
components._body:
Account managers run the weekly check-ins on three assigned engagements each. The lead [Tomás Reis](../people/tomas-reis.md) does not run weekly check-ins himself but reviews the notes and intervenes when an engagement is sliding (outline-roles-2025).

The weekly check-in is the rhythm of an Outline engagement; it's where scope drifts get caught, where client approvals get chased, and where the discipline lead is pulled in if the work needs adjustment (outline-roles-2025).
components.ai_effect: Status auto-summary from project tools. The lead intervenes only on flagged drift.

Coordinate the implementation or scheduling of validation testing with affected departments and personnel.
Direct validation activities, such as protocol creation or testing.

components.label: Context steward
components._description: A role that owns the studio's accumulated context on each client — positioning, visual language, brand book, market findings — and feeds it forward into every next engagement. Keeps prior work queryable instead of buried in delivered files.
components.ai_effect: A candidate role that doesn't exist today. AI makes it feasible — the studio's prior-engagement context could become a system instead of memory in three people's heads — but it has to be staffed and built. The map shows where it would sit, not that it's been built.

decisions.question: Where does the value of an Outline engagement actually sit?
decisions.answer:
The studio sells the strategy → identity → digital product flow as a single fixed-price bundle. Look at where each piece of the work is custom craft versus common practice that everyone in the category shares. Roughly two-thirds of an engagement — kickoff workshops, weekly check-ins, asset handovers, UI design, design-system documentation — is competent practice the studio shares with every other shop. The studio does not differentiate here. The differentiated value lives in three places only: writing the positioning document (Marco), defining the visual language and building the brand book (Lena, not delegated). About a quarter of the work carries one hundred percent of the differentiation.

Move: name the three differentiated pieces explicitly at pitch. The price stays one number; the conversation about what the client is paying for changes.

decisions.question: For what should the studio actually be paid?
decisions.answer:
Charging the same fixed price for irreplicable craft and for common-practice production hides the value. The deeper reframe is to separate the work by feedback speed and the amount of expert judgment each piece needs.

The brand book and the positioning are slow-feedback work — the verdict comes 12 to 24 months later, when the client is in the market and the artefact either holds up or doesn't. High judgment, irreplicable context. Price these as engagement-and-retention; sell annual updates of the brand-book and positioning as a follow-on retainer to past clients.

UI design and design-system documentation are fast-feedback — ship the screens, see what works the same week. Less expert judgment is needed. As AI matures these are the pieces that become market-standard first; clients can get them elsewhere or auto-generate them. Price them as production capacity, or include them as part of a larger upstream engagement so the differentiated work is what the client pays for.

The pricing is not where to add euros. It is what the studio chooses to take responsibility for.

decisions.question: Where does AI standardise the work first, and what's the funnel?
decisions.answer:
The production-side activities — UI design, design-system-build, ux-research synthesis — are where competitors will offer AI-augmented or AI-generated equivalents inside 18 months. Inside the studio's bundle these are vulnerable; standalone they are already market-standard.

This is not a threat to defend against. It is the funnel.

Move: announce a 'design system handoff' that the studio offers at zero margin, or gifted, when paired with a strategy + identity engagement. Use the standardised layer as the path that brings the client to the differentiated layer. The strategy bills well; the production layer becomes the giveaway that wins the strategy work in the first place.

decisions.question: Which roles need to shift?
decisions.answer:
Senior designers and senior product designers today run activities that are about to drift to market-standard. Their seniority is currently spent on production-side work — competent, well-executed, but not where the studio sells.

The shift: senior time moves upstream. Pair seniors with strategy on positioning briefs. Have seniors author brand-book chapters. Have seniors mentor juniors who handle the productized parts. The junior development arc the charter already describes is the right primitive for this transition; what is missing is the explicit re-allocation of senior hours away from production and toward judgment.

This is not a layoff conversation. It is a reallocation conversation, and operations should run it as a quarterly review of how senior hours are being spent.

decisions.question: What role is missing as the studio scales?
decisions.answer:
With value shifting upstream and AI handling more of the production layer, the role the studio does not yet have is a *context steward*: someone whose job is to keep the studio's accumulated knowledge of each client legible and current. Each engagement leaves behind a positioning, a visual language, a brand book, a set of decisions. Today these live in delivered files and the discipline leads' heads.

When AI augments execution, the defensible studio asset becomes the contextual ontology of each client engagement, maintained over time. The next hire is not a production lead (the obvious answer when you look at vendor management). It is the role that owns this client-context knowledge and lets it compound across engagements.

Name it Context Lead, Knowledge Steward, Engagement Memory Owner — the title matters less than the function. This is the role that ages best as the studio scales toward the 30-person cap.
